nodes.label: Ultimate POS as System of Record
nodes.rationale: There must be no second product catalog, customer master, payment ledger, tax engine, or aggregate stock engine; Recommerce is a domain capability inside one POS system, not a second application.

nodes.label: Integrated POS Experience Contract
nodes.rationale: Operator journey must stay continuous: shared shell, contacts, products, payments and accounting, with Customer Repairs and Stock & Devices as distinct operator contexts rather than separate products.

nodes.label: Canonical Physical Device (one row per unit)
nodes.rationale: Variation is a catalog option shared by quantities, PurchaseLine is a cost/lot layer, and sell_line_note is free text that cannot enforce identity; one row per unit in any of those would distort prices, reports and stock algorithms.

nodes.label: Ownership / Custody / Lifecycle / Stock-Participation Separation
nodes.rationale: Conflating who owns a device with who holds it and whether it counts as stock produces wrong POS quantities; customer ownership must always imply stock_participation=NONE.

nodes.label: Modular Monolith Deployment Shape
nodes.rationale: No microservices are justified for Alpha because atomic stock/device updates require the same database transaction and the installed queue defaults to synchronous execution.

nodes.label: Modules/Recommerce Implementation Boundary
nodes.rationale: An implementation boundary, not a user-facing system boundary: routes render inside the native POS layout and navigation is added to the native sidebar.

nodes.label: Provider Modules/Repair Containment Decision
nodes.rationale: The provider Repair module is unavailable, so SaverBro's owned Repair domain lives inside Modules/Recommerce; provider recovery matters only for legacy containment, data preservation and cutover safety.

nodes.label: Per-Variation Serialization Profiles
nodes.rationale: Tracked and untracked units must never silently mix, so LEGACY_MIXED holds an explicit exception quantity and a variation cannot reach TRACKED_REQUIRED until reconciliation passes.

nodes.label: Serialized Stock Coordinator
nodes.rationale: A single application service enforces the ten-step lock/validate/post/assert sequence so controllers cannot duplicate partially-correct stock logic.

nodes.label: Purchase Serialisation Guard
nodes.rationale: Attaching device evidence to an existing received purchase line closes the stock-identity gap without double-posting the POS ledger; the command returns core_stock_changed=false.

nodes.label: Core POS Integration Seams and Hooks
nodes.rationale: Prefer existing hooks (after_sale_saved, PurchaseCreatedOrModified, StockAdjustmentCreatedOrModified, StockTransferCreatedOrModified) and never fork ProductUtil/TransactionUtil into the module.

nodes.label: StockTransferController::updateStatus() Missing Event Gap
nodes.rationale: The core transfer status path dispatches no event, so tracked transfers cannot be guarded without adding a pre-commit event or module guard.

nodes.label: Shared Repair Engine with Job-Type Discriminator
nodes.rationale: One repair engine and one job table with INTERNAL_REFURBISHMENT / CUSTOMER_REPAIR keeps diagnostics, actions, parts and QC shared; type-specific policies are strategies, not duplicated tables or controllers.

nodes.label: Parts Reservation and Available-to-Promise
nodes.rationale: Reservation prevents double allocation without altering the accounting quantity; ATP = POS qty_available minus active Recommerce reservations.

nodes.label: Dual Parts Posting Strategy (Sale vs Stock Adjustment)
nodes.rationale: Customer jobs consume stock through the linked final POS sale and its FIFO/LIFO mapping; internal jobs post a standard stock adjustment with a unique source key, so the POS decrement remains the only consumption path.

nodes.label: Append-Only Recommerce Cost Ledger
nodes.rationale: One immutable source-linked ledger targeting exactly one device or job keeps estimated quote cost and actual cost from ever being conflated; revenue and payment stay in Ultimate POS.

nodes.label: Labour Costing Method (Open Human Decision)
nodes.rationale: Actual payroll cost, standard technician rate, or contribution-margin-only reporting are all defensible, so method and rate version must be stored with each entry until SaverBro decides.

nodes.label: Domain Events, Audit and Outbox
nodes.rationale: Spatie activity logging is operator-facing and generic, so the permanent timeline must never be derived solely from it; optional work is dispatched from an outbox row created in the same transaction.

nodes.label: Concurrency and Idempotency Controls
nodes.rationale: Unique indexes, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, lock_version, client command UUIDs and stable lock ordering together make retries safe and prevent double-posting.

nodes.label: Unsafe ReferenceCount Sequence Allocator
nodes.rationale: The existing read/increment is not concurrency-safe and lacks a unique (business_id, ref_type) index, so device and repair codes need their own locked unique sequence allocator.

nodes.label: Business-Scoped Permissions and Tenancy
nodes.rationale: Scan resolution is two-stage (exact identification, then authorization) and unauthorized users get a generic denial so token existence is never confirmed.

nodes.label: Failure Handling and Continuous Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Mismatches create blocking exceptions and manager-visible cases; no automatic balancing entry is made without evidence.
